pageCache.text:
A place where play matters An inclusive, nurturing community where everybody thrives
Thoughts from our parents.....
"We visited a number of Nurseries when it came time to choose for our son. We were struck by the range of facilities available at Bognor Regis Nursery School (as well as the outstanding grade from Ofsted) and felt that there was little chance he would ever find himself bored. The garden space is fabulous and changes throughout the year, while the indoors space offers such a range of activities and freedom for imagination that our little boy loves it and asks every day 'is it a nursery day today?' He spent a year in the Orchard Room before moving up to 'big nursery' and the transition was seamless, definitely aided by the 'free flow' that allowed him to go back and visit his old buddies and key worker group should he wish. We have loved our key workers and feel the relationship we and our son have built with them is a cherished one that enables open discussion, problem solving and team working for the good of our child."
"My son has absolutely thrived at Bognor Regis Nursery School. His development has been incredible. He has formed some amazing relationships with staff and especially his keyworker. He has additional needs and the SSC has supported him and has taught him so much. He's so happy there and looks forward to returning every day. I couldn't of chose a better setting for our boy."

pageCache.pageTitle: Bognor Regis Nursery School - The History of Bognor Regis Nursery School
pageCache.text:
The History of Bognor Regis Nursery School
Did you know Bognor Regis Nursery School began during World War II, caring for children evacuated from London and to look after children whose parents were needed in the war effort. Our very first home was at The Shrubbery on Upper Bognor Road… before moving to Victoria Drive on 1st July 1946. 80-years of serving our community!
I am incredibly proud to be part of a school with such a rich history. Miss Elger dedicated 27 years as Head of School from 1951 to 1978, and it is an honour to follow in the footsteps of such committed leaders.
Having started as Head of School in January 2026, I feel very fortunate to lead such a special school community. The responsibility is huge, but I am supported by an amazing team of skilled, dedicated and passionate staff who work tirelessly to ensure that every child receives the care, nurture and learning opportunities they deserve. Together, we are helping to build strong foundations for our children, creating happy memories and supporting them to flourish.
Whilst looking through old photos of Bognor Regis Nursery School, we discovered something very special… our original registers from 1946. These date back to the very year we moved to Victoria Drive—80 years ago!
It’s amazing to think how many children have been part of our nursery family over the years… and how that story is still continuing today.
Miss Elgar on the right, Mre Bennett on the left
We have a very special rocking horse here at Bognor Regis Nursery School. It’s the original rocking horse from when we moved to Victoria Drive 80 years ago!
Even more amazing… children are still enjoying playing on it today.
If you look closely at the back of the old photo, you can spot it—still part of our nursery life all these years later!

pageCache.pageTitle: Bognor Regis Nursery School - Curriculum & Ethos
pageCache.text:
Curriculum & Ethos
At Bognor Regis Nursery School, children are at the heart of everything we do. Our child‑led approach encourages them to follow their interests, ask questions, and explore the world with curiosity and confidence.
Through rich, thoughtfully planned experiences linked to the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), children are supported to develop deep, meaningful learning. They investigate, problem‑solve, and collaborate with others as they build on what they already know.
Our continuous provision is carefully designed to promote independence, giving children the freedom to make choices and take ownership of their learning. This empowers them to develop a love of discovery that helps them flourish both now and in the future.

Early Years Pupil Premium
What is the Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP)?
EYPP is a sum of money allocated to each Nursery School on a termly basis for eligible 9 month, 2, 3 & 4 year old children accessing their free entitlement in the Nursery that fulfil the criteria as set out by the DfE (Department for Education).
Children will be eligible for EYPP if they meet at least one of the following criteria:
Their family receives one of the following:
The Department for Education states:
“The aim of the Early Years Pupil Premium is to close the gap between children from disadvantaged backgrounds and their peers by providing funding to early years providers to help them raise the quality of their provision....Providers will use this funding most effectively where they have the flexibility to innovate and to spend it on the strategies that they think will be most effective”
The Pupil Premium is additional funding and it will be used by the Nursery Schools to address inequalities by ensuring that funding reaches the pupils who need it most.
Income Support
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-based Employment and Support Allowance
The guaranteed element of State Pension Credit
Universal Credit
How is it Spent?
Pupil Premium money will be used flexibly across each Nursery School in a variety of ways in order to address the needs of children at any one time. This could be by:
How the funding is used will be determined by each Nursery School, according to the needs of the individual children attending the Nursery who are in receipt of Early Years Pupil Premium Funding and therefore may change from term to term.
Providing small group work
Providing some 1-1 opportunities during the session
Providing additional equipment
Children who are Looked After
The Nursery Schools will liaise carefully with the ‘virtual school’ and the child’s Social Worker to decide how the money will be spent to maximise impact for the individual child.
How Do We Monitor Impact?
Evidence that the funding is having an impact on children’s progress will be found through discussions between staff and parents/carers, in children’s Learning Journals.

pageCache.text:
Links to useful SEND services
The links below are useful organisations, to support families :
Reaching Families is a parent-carer led, grassroots charity which aims to support parents and families of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in their daily lives, in particular through the delivery of information, training and peer support.
We’re a clinician-led company that believes Autism and ADHD assessments should always be carried out in-person and to a high standard.
We help families in Sussex to overcome their difficulties and prevent crisis. We support families struggling with issues such as poverty, ill health, learning difficulties, bereavement, family break-up and domestic abuse.
We offer full-time, term-based provision, either in-person at Centres or at Red Balloon of the Air, which offers a hybrid of online and face-to-face support (up to 15 hours per week).
Our approach puts wellbeing at the core of our students’ education experience, with a strong emphasis on mental health, personal development and positive social interaction alongside academic teaching.
At Aspens we provide high quality care and support to people on the autism spectrum and with learning disabilities; and their families; meeting their needs and aspirations and empowering them to learn and grow through an integrated network of services across the South-East.
WSPCF is an independent charity for the parent carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND).
We support parent carers by providing information, signposting, and training that equips them in their lifelong caring role and empowers them to participate in shaping services for their children and young people.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bognor Regis Nursery School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Governors
As a Local Authority Maintained Nursery School, we have a governing body in the same way that all other schools do.
Our governors come from various backgrounds, including staff members, parents and members of the local community with an interest in early years education. We are fortunate to have several governors from a teaching background which ensures that children's educational experiences are central to the work of the governing body. We also have governors with specific expertise in finance, community engagement and health and safety.
The governing body meet every half term to discuss and make decisions on matters such as finance, policies, staffing, resources, quality and standards and many other issues affecting the running of the Centre. Since the summer term 2017 the governors have decided that every meeting will involve the full governing body. This decision has removed the need for separate committee meetings, ensuring that information is shared more effectively across the whole governing body and providing coherent strategic oversight of the Centre.
​If you would like to contact a member of the governing body, please do so using the Bognor Nursery contact details.
You can view the current Governor pro forma here :
Ruth Campbell - Executive Head Teacher
Vikki Cripps - Head of School
​Sophie Elsdon - Chair of Governors & Local Authority Governor
​Abigail Blumzon - Vice Chair Co-opted
Abigail is a Chartered Project Manager and Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (FRICS), with over a decade of experience leading complex construction and building safety projects. She currently leads the South Coast Project Management team at a consultancy called Bailey Partnership and is passionate about creating safe, inclusive, and well-managed environments for communities.
As Vice Chair of Governors, Abigail brings a strong focus on strategic leadership, governance, and accountability. She is particularly interested in supporting staff development, ensuring robust health and safety practices, and strengthening the long-term sustainability of the Federation.
Abigail is also an active member of her local community and a parent, and is committed to ensuring that nursery settings provide nurturing, inclusive environments where every child can thrive.
Teresa Matthewson - Clerk to Governors
Clare Blanchard- Co-opted
Nicola Nield - Staff Governor
Nicola has been a Staff Governor since 2022 and has been part of the Boundstone team since 2013. She began her journey as a Nursery Nurse, working closely with children aged 3-4, supporting their early development and learning.
In 2024 Nicola took on a new post in the office as Finance Assistant, while still supporting in the nursery when needed. This dual role allows her to maintain a strong connection with both the operational and educational aspects of the setting.
This unique position supports Nicola to understand how the nursery operates from a range of perspectives and contribute effectively within the framework of the Governing Body.
​Angela Bradley- Co-opted
Angela became a Governor at the end of 2025. This is her first such role having undertaken a range of voluntary positions previously ranging from chairperson of homeowner’s associations to operating a hyperbaric chamber!
During the day Angela is a technical advisor to R&D projects working on malaria, principally in sub–Saharan Africa. She holds a PhD in Medical Entomology from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine and lived overseas for a large proportion of her career.
Previously she supported a vocational school in Uganda providing support both strategic and financial to staff, students and the charitable benefactors.
In recent years Angela has finally settled down as a wife and mother and enjoys the finer things in life, mainly her home and garden.
Vicki Ayles - Co-opted
​Aedan Kerney- Co-opted
Aedan worked as a teacher in Lancing for forty-one years and in his retirement directs two local choirs. He became a governor at Boundstone Nursery School in 2009 and his own two children attended the Nursery in the 1970s. He is passionate about the importance of Early Years Education.
Tom Rogers- Co-opted

The Local Offer
Since September 2014, every Local Authority has been required to publish information about available services for children who have special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). This is known as the ‘Local Offer’. This easy to understand information will set out what is normally available in schools and early years settings (e.g. playgroups and day nurseries) to support children with additional needs. It is not simply a list of services, but provides useful information on how to access services, any eligibility criteria, how decisions are made and who makes them.
Additionally, as a Maintained School we are required to publish further information in a SEND report which can be found below.
Please click below to read about our own offer for children with additional needs or to go to the West Sussex County Council Local Offer website.
